newsitem.title: USA: US Senate Finance chair disappointed with tax cut.
newsitem.headline: US Senate Finance chair disappointed with tax cut.

text.p: The chairman of the Senate Finance Committee said Friday he was "disappointed" with the size of the tax cut in the budget agreement between congressional leaders and the White House.
"I do not know all of the details of the agreement, but I must say that I am disappointed by the small size of the tax cut," Sen William Roth, a Delaware Republican, said in a statement.
The budget accord includes $85 billion in net tax cuts over five years. Roth had been pushing for $140 billion net tax cuts over five years.
